title: Kaplan trigger curve for deployment safety
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Ship a flexible, cohort-aware automated rollback trigger (the "Kaplan trigger curve") that fuses latency, error rate, per-request token cost, and throughput signals into a single trigger score. The adapter should be configur able per-deployment and support staged rollouts (shadow, 0.1%, 1%, 5%, 25%) with tunable hysteresis and confidence weighting so we avoid noisy false positives while still catching regressions that matter to customer SLAs and unit economics.

Why this is needed: Current canary guardrails depend on static thresholds per metric. We see two gaps: (1) cost regressions (token inflation) are frequently overlooked by latency/error-based gates and (2) small traffic cohorts with high variance can either block safe rollouts or be ignored. The Kaplan trigger curve is intended to normalize signals by traffic and sample confidence and provide an explainable score used by the rollout orchestrator to auto-evacuate or throttle traffic.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement UI for rule editing (Console work will follow) and does not change existing SLO definitions — it consumes SLO-derived signals and user-configured weights only.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A trigger adapter service that ingests the streaming metrics feed (latency p50/p95/p99, error_rate, tokens_per_request, rps) and emits a single per-cohort trigger_score per minute.
2) Config schema allowing weights for each signal, a minimum cohort-confidence threshold, and a traffic-fraction floor.
3) Unit and integration tests covering injected anomaly scenarios (latency-only, cost-only, combined).
4) Simulation harness that replays last 90 days of production traffic and demonstrates recall >= 90% for historical incidents while keeping false positive rate < 3% on baseline traffic.
5) Dashboard tile and runbook links created; rollout orchestrator (canary controller) reacts to trigger_score > configured_threshold by initiating automatic evacuation path documented in playbook.
tasks:
- Design and PRD (Asha): finalize signal weighting UX and default curves.
- Metrics adaptor (Luca): implement ingestion, normalization, and scoring pipeline.
- Simulation harness (Data Eng): build replay job and scenario injection.
- Integration (Infra): wire scoring output to canary controller / webhook.
- Tests (QA): create chaos scenarios and assert correct evacuations.
- Docs (Solutions): runbook and Confluence design note.
- Observability (SRE): add tracing, traces-per-trigger metrics, SLI for trigger latency.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (shadow): run Kaplan trigger curve in shadow for 2 weeks on 100% traffic (no automated evacuations) and compare trigger events with existing manual incidents. Phase 2 (slow canary): enable automated evacuations at traffic fractions <= 1% with conservative threshold and long hysteresis windows. Phase 3 (wider rollout): increase to 5-25% traffic and begin automatic throttles alongside canary rollouts; promote to default for all model rollouts after 90 days of stable performance and playbook signoff.
instrumentation:
- Required metrics: latency_p50/p95/p99, error_rate, tokens_per_request, rps per-cohort.
- Derived signals: cohort_confidence (based on sample size and variance), cost_normalized_delta (tokens_per_request / baseline_tokens), weighted_trigger_score.
- Telemetry: expose trigger_score histogram, time-to-trigger, false_positive_rate gauge, and last_action_taken tag.
- Logs: structured events on every emitted trigger_score and action (no-op/shadow/evacuate) with request sample ids for traceability.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for scoring math and edge cases (zero traffic, extreme token spikes).
2) Replay tests: run 10 synthetic incident scenarios through the simulation harness and validate the controller decision.
3) Live shadow run: compare signals to PagerDuty incidents and manual rollbacks over two weeks.
4) Game day: simulate partial mesh failure + model quality regression to validate combined-signal detection and safe evacuation path.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: noisy cohorts cause churn -> Mitigation: require minimum cohort_confidence and employ exponential backoff on repeated triggers.
- Risk: cost normalization hides true latency regressions -> Mitigation: require per-signal minimum weight and veto if latency_p99 exceeds emergency ceiling.
- Risk: incorrect defaults lead to missed incidents -> Mitigation: conservative defaults + mandatory shadow period before auto-evacuations.
- Risk: permissioning and cross-tenant rules -> Mitigation: restrict automatic evacuations to tenant-scoped controllers and add audit log entries for every action.
